content.title: About
content.content: Squash is a summer vegetable with a bright yellow color, belonging to the Cucurbitaceae family. It is commonly eaten raw with the skin on, which retains most of its nutrients. Squash has a mild, slightly sweet flavor and a crisp texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Squash belongs to the same family as pumpkin, cucumber, and watermelon.
There are more than 50 varieties of yellow summer squash, differing in shape, size, and shade.
The edible skin is rich in fiber and antioxidants, so it is usually left on.
Squash is widely used in Mediterranean and Asian cuisines.
In some regions it is called “summer pumpkin.”

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Low‑calorie source of fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and helps maintain satiety.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and supports heart function.

items.title: Source of folate
items.content: Folate is essential for cell division and especially important for pregnant women.

items.title: Antioxidant compounds
items.content: Carotenoids and lutein in squash protect the eyes from oxidative stress.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience an allergic reaction to squash.

items.title: Pesticide residue
items.content: Choose organic produce or wash thoroughly to reduce pesticide exposure.

items.title: Digestive issues
items.content: Large amounts of raw squash can cause gas in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Squash can be eaten raw in salads, sliced into thin ribbons as “zoodles,” added to smoothies, or used in fresh appetizers. The skin can be left on as it is tender and nutritious.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store squash in the refrigerator’s vegetable drawer, wrapped in a paper towel or in a perforated bag. It stays fresh for up to 5 days. Avoid high humidity to prevent spoilage.
